_meta.name: deep_space_profile
_meta.description: Multi-kingdom relative abundance vector for a spacecraft environment during extended deep-space transit (months from resupply). Represents the 'bottleneck' microbiome after prolonged isolation: reduced diversity, stronger human skin/gut dominance, loss of transient environmental taxa introduced during resupply. Analogous to open_ocean_profile.json for maritime platforms, this serves as the drift endpoint in the GRUMB ecological drift model.
_meta.basis: Derived from ISS longitudinal microbiome studies showing reduced diversity over time between resupply missions (Checinska Sielaff et al. 2019, Singh et al. 2018)
_meta.notes: Key differences from iss_baseline_profile: (1) Loss of cargo-introduced transients (Pantoea, Bacillus), (2) Increased dominance of obligate human commensals (Staphylococcus, Corynebacterium), (3) Reduced fungal diversity, (4) Possible accumulation of biofilm-forming organisms on surfaces. The ecological drift from baseline→deep_space represents the closed-system diversity decay that is a key feature of isolated habitat microbiome dynamics.

Fungi._note: Reduced fungal diversity during extended isolation. Rhodotorula and Aspergillus persist; transient cargo fungi decline.
